client_brief:
Personalised renewal postcards, including eleven correctly separated producer files

For Aldervale Mutual's autumn renewal drop, each household must receive its own address, offer band and assigned producer's photograph. The starting point is the printer's PDF and our spreadsheet.

Please treat the split files as part of the main job, not an afterthought. Each of the eleven producers must receive only their own households, and the record-selection method must guarantee that identity.

Mail-house and producer files
One press file for the mail house with page count exactly equal to the drop list's row count, one household per page in the order the file was merged, every page carrying that household's own address complete to its final line, its own offer band and its assigned producer's own photograph. Plus eleven per producer files, each named for its producer, each containing only that producer's households, with identity guaranteed by how the subset was requested.

Portrait preparation
Eleven producer portraits brought to one look across two shooting situations (one white point, one contrast, one head size in frame), knocked out onto the card's own ground with an edge that holds on the green rather than only against white, cropped to the template's real portrait proportion, named to the values the drop list binds by, and no output above its source frame's pixel dimensions. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log and the file to producer reconciliation.

Source material: aldervale_renewal_card_2025.pdf; aldervale_producers/ (11 portraits, 6000 x 4000); aldervale_households.csv; aldervale_producer_card.jpg; aldervale_brand_sheet.pdf; aldervale_offer_copy.txt.

Check the portrait edges on the card's green ground and crop to the real template proportion. Complete addresses must survive to their final line. We need a file-to-producer reconciliation and a clear explanation of any source limitation before the files are treated as ready for mailing.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it.

Please work within $1,400-$3,800 fixed and the 7 to 15 business days target. Allow for one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Anchored to the Freelancer.com brand-collateral post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note: a regional broker asking for a fixed brand-locked template populated from a structured roster into a press-ready PDF plus an editable source, insisting that 'the colors, fonts and overall layout from the brand style guide' come through clearly and that 'I don't want to hunt for missing fonts or mismatched data'. The real post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional carrier Aldervale Mutual Assurance; no real company, carrier, agency, person, product or trademark appears anywhere, and the earlier working name that collided with a live Rhode Island carrier is fully removed. The prior version of this engagement sat on the data merge alone, which is what the REBUILD verdict is about. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: a bare printer's PDF can now be reverse engineered into a live merge template headlessly, a per row image column genuinely binds a different photograph to every record, and an ink level trace off a photographed printed card recovers a real mark. So this is that broker's actual job, end to end: the template is recovered rather than assumed, the producers' faces are real faces, and the editable source they asked for exists.

price_band_and_audience: A mutual whose average home policy runs 1,100 to 1,900 dollars a year, sold face to face by a producer the household knows by name, to owners aged forty to seventy in towns under four thousand people. The band is load-bearing. At this register the card is restrained: one photograph, a serif voice, generous margins, the offer stated once and quietly, the producer's name larger than the offer. Push it down into the mass renewal blast register (bright panel, a percentage in the largest type on the card, three benefit bullets, a starburst) and a household insured here for thirty years reads it as churn marketing from a carrier that has stopped knowing them, which is exactly the retention the drop exists to protect. Push it up into private wealth register (cream stock feel, all small caps, no photograph, almost no offer) and it stops being a renewal reminder for a farmhouse policy. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Cover from people who know your town
brand_identity.sector: A regional mutual carrier writing home and farm cover, sold face to face through local producers across rural Vermont.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: central Vermont; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Aldervale Mutual Assurance is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is central Vermont, and this commission covers phase 2: personalised renewal mailer.
brand_identity.audience: Homeowners and farm owners aged forty to seventy in small Vermont towns, many insured here for decades, who value a known producer and a fair renewal over the lowest online quote.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Average home policy runs 1,100 to 1,900 dollars a year. Mid market and relationship led, not a discount carrier and not a private wealth boutique. Communications stay restrained: one photograph, generous margins, the offer stated once and quietly, the producer named larger than the offer.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet serif system as set in the 2019 style guide: a text serif for policy copy and addresses, paired with a slightly heavier serif for producer names and headings. Editorial rather than promotional, generous leading, no condensed or display faces.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct and adult. We write to the household, never at the market, and we never oversell. Example line the brand would write: "Your renewal is due in October, and your producer, will be glad to walk it through with you."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original design files are gone: the designer retired and took her drive, so the last renewal card survives only as the printer's press PDF. The mark exists cleanly only where it was printed on a producer's business card. One 2019 style guide page (house green, warm grey, the two type families, clear space, and the rule that the mark never sits on a photograph) is all the written guidance that remains.
brand_identity.values: Continuity and knowing the policyholder. Households should feel written to by a carrier that still knows them, and the mark is never placed over a photograph.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_renewal_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF of last spring's renewal postcard, held by the printer, single page, both sides, real embedded font subsets.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the card exactly as it printed last spring. It is the only form of the artwork that still exists."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the printed card visually separates into a salutation, an address block, a producer line and an offer band converts into far fewer frames than that, because the whole left column was set as one continuous flow, so the fields cannot be addressed as separate frames and must be reached by position inside a single story. Worse, the mapping readout of that story omits one run entirely while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns VALID with no warnings, the placeholder step reports success, and the mappings past the omission are silently absent from the template.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_producers/ (11 portraits, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Producer headshots, some taken at the regional meeting against the hotel's cream function room wall, some taken later outside an office by a colleague on a full frame body.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our eleven producers. Taken at the regional meeting and afterwards by whoever had a camera, so they are a mixed bag."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The frames are far larger than the one call knockout expects, and that tool silently reduces oversized inputs while reporting it in no message and no error, only as a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoffs object. Separately, the four shot against the cream function room wall sit at almost the value of that wall at the shoulder and collar, so subject detection has no contrast there and returns a cut edge that looks clean against white and bites visibly once the cutout lands on the card's own green band. Three files are named for the branch office rather than the person, so which face belongs to which producer cannot be settled from the filenames.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_households.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The cleaned drop list: about sixty rows carrying household name, address lines, town, state, ZIP, assigned producer and renewal offer band.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's list, cleaned. Sixty homes in this drop."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A dozen or so households carry a materially longer address than the rest: a second line, an apartment or unit designator, a long town name, a rural route. The card's address frame is fixed and does not spill or reflow, so those records do not push the layout, they simply stop rendering partway and lose their last line at trim while the merge reports complete success. Two offer band strings are also much longer than the rest for the same reason. Nothing in the sheet marks these rows.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_producer_card.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of a printed agency business card lying on a desk, the mark on it in two inks on uncoated stock: an oak leaf inside a shield ring, set beside small caps type and separated by a hairline rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean version of our mark left. One of the producers still had this card in his wallet."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup photographed on a substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A prompt naming the card returns the card. A prompt naming the whole lockup returns the type and silently drops the shield ring and the hairline rule while looking entirely plausible. Background removal on the shield returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched, and the trace that does work arrives with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it. The two inks also run close in value along the shadowed right edge of the card.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_brand_sheet.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: One page from the 2019 style guide: the house green and the secondary warm grey, the two type families by name, the mark's minimum clear space and the rule that the mark never sits on a photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our style guide page. Please keep to it."

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_offer_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the four offer band sentences as approved by the carrier's compliance reviewer, the renewal deadline, and the standing regulatory line that must appear on every card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The offer wording as compliance approved it. None of this can be reworded."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the template the client's own PDF produces can actually hold all of the card's fields. The mapping readout for this document omits one text run entirely while keeping its line break, so the story string it hands back still reads as well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns VALID with zero warnings on those offsets, the placeholder step returns completed successfully, and the fields past the omission are simply absent from the prepared template. Which run is omitted, and therefore which fields fall off the end, is a property of this converted document and appears in no response, warning or error. It is visible only by round tripping the prepared document and reading its story against the card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the omission is inside the only readout the tools offer and every mapping strategy consumes that readout. Doing it right first time presumes already knowing that this document's readout drops a run, which is document specific. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a card carrying each household's own details and says nothing about how the artwork converts, and the acceptance line about every field landing is the client's requirement rather than a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different derivation of the mapping, computed from reconstructed content runs rather than from the readout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the round tripped document's own content runs, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild the mapping, prepare again and verify field by field by inspection rather than by response, before any record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Sixty renewal cards printed and mailed with the producer line and the offer line missing, after a run in which the validator, the preparation step and the merge all reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What this list does to this card. The address frame is fixed and does not spill or reflow, so a household whose address runs longer than last year's typical row does not push the layout or throw an error: the frame stops rendering partway and the record loses its final line at trim, postal code included, while the merge reports every record complete. Which households this happens to depends on the frame's real bounds and set size against each row's actual string, and no readout reports it. It exists only on the rendered pages, and only on some of them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the frame cannot be resized through this surface at all; the fit is only discoverable once real rows are set in the real frame. (b) Nothing states it: the list is described as cleaned, and the acceptance line about complete address blocks is the standing requirement of any mail run rather than a warning that some will truncate. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a per record copy fit decision, which is different work from merging again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every page rather than the first, name the households that will not set, decide per record whether the address can be legitimately fitted (a combined line, a standard state abbreviation, a dropped unit prefix) or whether the record has to be flagged back to the carrier, apply those decisions to the data, merge again and re-read the affected pages.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A dozen or more cards going to the mail house with the postal line missing, which the mail house will either return or post undeliverable, in the one drop of the year that exists to keep long standing households from leaving.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one call knockout gives back a portrait the card can use. Two things are reported nowhere except inside the returned tradeoffs object: the tool silently reduces these oversized frames and does not restore the size afterwards, so a plate can come back below what the card's portrait frame needs, and the only route back is interpolation, which the crop tool performs to a hard cap while again saying so only in its own tradeoffs. Separately, the frames shot against the cream function room wall carry almost no value difference at the shoulder and collar, so a cut edge that looks clean against white bites visibly once the plate sits on the card's green band. Which of the eleven behave this way is a property of each frame's own contrast, and neither fact appears in any success message.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it: the defensible sequence is straighten, correct, knock out at source scale and only then crop, precisely so the edge is judged after it exists, and there is no parameter that controls the reduction or reads ahead to it. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the portraits are a mixed bag, and the acceptance line about edges holding on the green is the client's standing quality requirement. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different route per frame, an explicitly selected and inverted ground filled to the house colour rather than a one call knockout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route frame by frame, re-derive the affected plates through an explicit selection of the wall by its own material properties, inverted and filled, re-inspect each cut edge on the green rather than on white, and re-read both the reduction and the upscale entries in every tradeoffs object before any plate is bound.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Four producers appearing on their own neighbours' mail with a chewed collar and a halo against the house green, or eleven portraits brought to frame size by interpolation and printed soft at postcard scale.

decision_gates: Whether the template the client's own artwork produces can carry the fields the card shows, which the printed card cannot tell you and the readout will not tell you honestly.
Whether to author the mapping against the readout's convenient string or against the document's own reconstructed text.
Which of the three ambiguously named portrait files belongs to which producer, settled from faces and towns rather than filenames.
Knockout route per portrait: the one call route where shoulder contrast supports it, an explicitly selected and inverted ground filled to the house colour where it does not.
The portrait crop proportion, which is set by the converted template's real frame bounds rather than by what the printed card appears to show.
How the master file is ordered for the mail house, given that a producer's contiguous block and the mail house's order are two different sorts and only one can live in one file.
Per household copy fitting on the longest addresses: what can be legitimately shortened in a postal address and what has to be flagged back to the carrier instead.
Which mark variant carries the card, judged at reproduction size on the green rather than at full canvas.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of an insurance postcard. IDENTITY: these are eleven real producers whose actual faces have to appear on the mail going to their own towns, and the mark has to be RECOVERED off a photographed business card rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different carrier's mark on a regulated communication. SPEC: sixty households each need their own address, their own producer and their own compliance approved offer line, delivered as one press file whose page count equals the row count and as eleven correctly partitioned per producer files, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the digital set exists because the offer dates move every year and the carrier explicitly intends to change it itself.
